name: translatable-field
title: Translatable field
description: One field in many languages: a tab per language with a clear missing mark, so editors see what is translated and what is not.
docs: locales is the list of { code, label }; defaultLocale (default: the first) is the source language: it is moved to the front, it is what required applies to and what Copy from copies from. value is a record such as { en: "Welcome", nl: "Welkom" } and onValueChange gets the whole record on every change; a language that is emptied loses its key. Each tab says where its language stands in an icon and words: a check when filled, a dash and Missing when empty, Required for the default language when required is set, or Over limit; the tabs wrap onto a second line when the languages do not fit, and a screen reader hears each as its code, its language and where it stands (NL, Nederlands filled), so a voice command that says the code on show finds the tab. maxLength is a guide and not a wall (a German translation is often longer than its English source): a longer text is allowed, counted in red and marked on its tab. A line above the tabs says how many languages are filled. In any other language the default text is shown above the field with a Copy from English button that fills the field and offers Undo for a few seconds. The tabs use manual activation: arrow keys move focus between them, Enter, Space or a click chooses one and the focus goes into the field, ready to write in that language. locale and onLocaleChange let several fields on one form follow the same language. With name, each language also goes out in a hidden input called name[code]; a hidden input has no native required check, so validate required in your schema and set invalid to show the result. labels carries every word.
